meta.title: Three Notes Is the Whole Chord
meta.summary: A triad is a complete chord, not a fragment of one — root, third and fifth, and nothing missing.

spans.text: Three notes is a whole chord. Not a sketch of one, not the easy version you play until you learn the real thing — the real thing itself. If you think of a chord as a shape your fingers make, this is the lesson that replaces that picture with a shorter, truer one: a chord is a set of notes, and the smallest set that counts is three.
: a root, a third above it, and a fifth above the root. Over
. The chords you already play are built around a three-note core like this one; everything else added on top is decoration.
What decides whether a triad sounds major, minor, diminished, or augmented is not a different shape — it's two stacked intervals. Major stacks
Here's C major on the top three strings, root position — three dots, three notes, nothing left out.

props.caption: C major, root position, strings 1-2-3 — three dots are the whole chord.

spans.text: Those three dots aren't a summary of the chord. They're the chord. Nothing about this grip is incomplete — it has a root, a third, and a fifth, which is the entire definition of a major triad.
So what's a six-string barre chord, if three notes is already everything? The same three notes, some of them repeated. Take an
, low string to high. Read the pitches and you get
— six voices, but only three names.

. The barre chord doesn't add a fourth note name to the triad — it doubles three of the ones already there, spread across six strings for volume and weight. The three-note grip above and this six-string barre are the same chord. One of them is just louder.
A three-string chord isn't a fragment of a "real" six-string chord. It's the other way round: the barre chord is the triad with some of its notes copied.
This pathway leans on one notation, established here so it never needs re-explaining. A grip is written as a six-slot chart, low E first, with
for a string that isn't played. The root-position grip above is
— always six slots, even though only three of them have a number in them.
A single position inside a grip is written string, then fret:
means string 3, fret 5 — spelled out in words this once so the shorthand is never ambiguous again. String 1 is the high
. Every chart and every diagram in this pathway counts strings that same way.
, you already know the neck is a map you can move around on — that's a recommended head start here, not a requirement, and nothing in this pathway assumes you've done it.

Next: a triad's three notes don't have to stack root-third-fifth from the bottom up. Which one ends up lowest changes where the grip sits on the neck — but not, as it turns out, what the chord is called.
